title: Turning a quiet FrogPop showcase into a frantic survival challenge
author: PerspectivePersonal
selftext:
I'm developing FrogPop, a bubble-popping arcade roguelite, with AI assistance in production and some of the artwork. This clip came out of an AI-assisted capture and editing workflow, with each revision directed and reviewed by me.



The first version had the frog dodging only a couple of bubbles, which missed the pressure of the game. Increasing the density made it hectic, but also made the action hard to read. I then requested several reductions in ordinary bubbles while keeping the frog attacking and moving.



The more useful changes were specific: put the lightning chains first, make the lily-pad ricochets chaotic, freeze a larger cluster with ice, and show the actual flood event raising the water in the stone section. Shortening the four sections brought the whole clip to 12 seconds. The lesson from these iterations was that asking AI for 'more hectic' needed concrete constraints about what the viewer should be able to see.



This is staged development-build gameplay with arranged encounters and scripted inputs at normal game speed, not a human clutch run or typical demo difficulty. AI also helped prepare this post.



The free Windows demo has 10 waves and two bosses, with a smaller content selection than this showcase: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=organic\_social&utm\_campaign=special\_bubbles\_20261125&utm\_content=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5067810/FrogPop/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=special_bubbles_20261125&utm_content=aigamedev)
